verdict.rationale: First-party docs show Keycloak is run on your own infrastructure. They cover a docker run quickstart, running from a container image, installing via the Kubernetes/OpenShift Operator, switching to a production database like PostgreSQL, putting it behind a reverse proxy, and clustering. Community users independently report running it self-hosted for years in Docker and in clusters, though some note heavy memory use and OpenShift friction. Missing for 10: an explicit open-source license or self-hosting terms statement in the evidence, and mixed community reports on resource weight and container ergonomics.
